findings.statement: Original final assembly restamps a changed synthetic wrapper payload while retaining its prior approved basis; no actual production corruption asserted.
Actual old scan resolves case-insensitive inventory naming, both wrapper path forms, exact user exclusions, ignored selections and six appended original identities.
Expected identity map carries wrapper, prior audit, raw, preimage and installed receipt pins through final assets; conflicting identities and final drift refuse.
Proposed actual local scan passed with nineteen closed wrappers, 2511 assets, 87 ignored/untracked payloads and exactly six approved originals, without staging.
Inventory snapshots are selected from pinned prior audit and final installation/preimage receipts; new unbound files fail instead of wildcard admission.
The optional future CI receipt must be closed-wrapper bound with its schema and installed-file pins. Actual CI branch awaits a reviewed receipt; only unbound refusal is covered here.

limitations: Actual scan requires the fixed repository, HEAD and source metadata; the closed audit verifier itself uses only copied payloads.
No canonical corruption, legal truth, later staging or publication is certified.
Other maintained file selections are observed snapshots unless independently installation-bound.
Future CI receipt and schema must be reviewed and exactly pinned before use; actual CI installation was absent during this successful scan.
This bounded revision does not comprehensively harden ancestor symlinks or general wrapper authorization.
The source scanner and proposed revision retain one-off formatting; no maintained module was edited.
